reason: Remove scenario opening facts not stated in canonical Japanese (low disposal, an exact ten-bag order, discounted-set sales increase); retain canonical operational sequence.

changes.before: Costs rise despite little disposal. Checking deliveries and stocktakes, the supervisor finds a price per kg entered as a price per bag and corrects units and valuation. Separate real cost increases from recording errors and use distinct measures for portion checks and data-entry checks.
changes.after: The supervisor checks deliveries and stocktakes as well as the quantity discarded. A price per kg has been entered as a price per bag for one item, so the supervisor corrects the quantity unit and inventory valuation. Separate actual cost increases from recording errors, and address portion checks and data-entry checks as distinct measures.

changes.before: Ten bags were ordered but twelve arrive, with a twelve-bag delivery note and good quality. The supervisor identifies the excess and, considering forecasts and storage capacity, declines it and adjusts quantities and billing with the supplier. Explain to the new worker that receipt checks prevent excess as well as shortages and retain the record.
changes.after: The delivery note also lists twelve bags and the quality is acceptable, but the supervisor confirms that the quantity exceeds the plan. Considering demand forecasts and storage capacity, the supervisor declines the excess and agrees quantity and billing adjustments with the supplier. Explain to the new worker that receipt checks prevent overdelivery as well as shortages, and retain the inspection record.

changes.before: Discounted set sales rise. The supervisor also checks substitution from regular items, gross profit and peak kitchen load. Longer waits lead to changes in set contents and selling periods. Promote return visits at payment and track next month’s visits and profit before judging effectiveness.
changes.after: The supervisor does not judge success solely by increased sales, but also checks substitution from regular items, gross profit and kitchen workload at peak times. Longer waits lead to adjustments to the set contents and serving times. At payment, staff encourage a return visit; the supervisor then tracks visits and profit through the following month to assess effectiveness.
